inputPreconditions: Observation and Gold use evaluationSchemaVersion 2 and have the same caseId.
attemptBudget is a non-negative integer; no-tool Gold has no allowed sequences.
Tool-positive Gold has unique non-empty sequences; each has unique step IDs and exactly one final terminal step.
Every prior-output binding references an earlier step in the same sequence.
Runtime contract IDs are unique; every Gold step references a present identity/operation-compatible contract with frozen integer acceptance statuses.
The public scorer throws on an input-precondition violation instead of turning bad data into a model outcome.
semanticInvariants: Only executor-bound attempts contribute to triggeredAttempt, observedAttemptCount, and FCR_attempt facts.

A complete chain is an ordered allowed-sequence match with per-step identity, operation, arguments, prior-output binding, exact referenced-contract identity, and terminal semantics; HTTP acceptance is not part of behavioral success.

Operation normalization distinguishes none, value, conflict, and invalid results; a present non-string argument selector is invalid, and conflict or invalid operations never match a Gold none/exact operation.
Unexpected, duplicate, or over-budget attempts can preserve completeChainSuccess but make strictChainExact false, positiveOvercall true, and ToolSPL smaller.

A forbidden wrong-family, typed wrong-terminal, or genuinely premature behavior-valid terminal before a correct terminal prevents later repair from creating terminalSelectionCorrect or completeChainSuccess.

The evaluation prefix stops at the earliest Gold terminal whose own arguments, binding, and exact referenced RuntimeToolContract identity are valid; a corrected prerequisite before that horizon may complete the chain, while a retry after the horizon cannot repair it.
runtimeAcceptedChain and runtimeAcceptedChainRate preserve HTTP/RuntimeToolContract acceptance as descriptive diagnostics and never change completeChainSuccess.
Without a terminal horizon, failed positives stop at budget or turn completion.
behaviorValidTerminalAttemptIndex is the sole executor-bound evaluation, usage, cache, and run-level infrastructure horizon ordinal; it is independent of complete-chain success and HTTP acceptance.
terminalAttemptIndex is a diagnostic executor-bound ordinal identifying the scored horizon/complete terminal, otherwise the Qi match, otherwise an in-prefix raw terminal candidate.
Post-terminal behavior does not change decision metrics, but raw trace and infrastructure facts remain preserved for Integration.
M0 never produces final formal metric eligibility.
formalDataBlockers: The exact task1-data-formal-v1.1 freeze is available, but M0 alone cannot make a run formalMetricEligible; R04 Integration must combine scorer facts with runtime, usage, isolation, and infrastructure evidence.
